text.p: French first division matches scheduled this weekend (standings in parentheses, all times GMT):

Early season leaders Lens are fighting desperate battle against relegation and, with only five points from last 11 games, will be happy if injury-depleted team gain away point. Lyon are unbeaten in last two games.

Nantes welcome back playmaker and top scorer Japhet N'Doram as they look to go 20 league games unbeaten in Breton derby against side with best home record in top flight but who may have to do without first choice centre-back partnership of Eric Decroix and Bruno Carotti, both nursing injuries.

Leaders Monaco will be looking to return to winning ways after going down 2-1 at Strasbourg in League Cup semifinal on Tuesday with coach Jean Tigana not hiding displeasure over mistakes at set pieces. Metz have lost last two games without scoring.

Guingamp will be looking to avoid becoming first team to lose to PSG at Parc des Princes since Lille on November 13. PSG ended worrying five-match run of league games with victory by winning 2-1 at Lens last weekend.

Marseille, chasing place in Europe next season, seek first away win of season and revenge for League Cup elimination by Bordeaux on same ground last month. Defender Hamada Jambay is suspended. Bordeaux, after two successive draws, will look for win to put them back among top three.

Corsican team, involved in race with PSG for second European Champions' League place, will be looking for maximum points from this match as well as game in hand at lowly Caen which was called off because of bad weather last weekend. Nancy go for second successive win.

Champions Auxerre, unbeaten in league this year, will be looking to keep pace with leaders while continuing to tune team for European Cup quarter-final agianst Borussia Dortmund next month. Relegation-threatened Montpellier must recover from disappointment of League Cup semifinal elimination in midweek.

League Cup finalists Strasbourg are in buoyant mood and could be forgiven for complaining that in-form striker David Zitelli -- 16 goals in league, five in League Cup -- has not been called up for France's international against Netherlands next week. Lille are licking wounds after 5-1 thrashing at Marseille.
Le Havre have not won for five matches and scored only twice. Cannes, who have weakest attack in top flight, are also winless this year with just one goal in 1-1 draw with PSG.
Clash of basement clubs with both looking for fourth win of season. Nice unbeaten at home since early November but have not won for four matches. Caen have drawn last two away games.
